output:
*Interview with Mademoiselle Lina Ruedi, régleuse, in the dining room. Second interview of the night.*

MATTHEY: Mademoiselle Ruedi, thank you for waiting. Please sit down. I would like you to tell me, in your own order, what you did this evening.

MLLE RUEDI: At dinner the master made us show our watches, as he does every year. He did it when the temple bell struck nine. Mine was exact. I regulated it myself, and I know what it does. Monsieur Félix's was twenty minutes behind. Monsieur Girard's was four minutes behind. The doctor's was two minutes ahead. The master told each of them what was wrong with it. He was generally right, which did not make the dinner more pleasant.

MATTHEY: And after dinner?

MLLE RUEDI: I went up to the atelier to work beside the master. We had a movement on the bench that needed the hairspring set. When the temple struck ten, the regulator on the wall agreed with the bell exactly.

MATTHEY: Did anything happen after that, before you went down?

MLLE RUEDI: He sent me downstairs when the regulator showed twenty past ten. The regulator was running then, and he was well. I want that understood, Monsieur.

MATTHEY: You mentioned the repeater. Can you tell me about it?

MLLE RUEDI: He had been at it four years. It is a minute repeater, so when you press the slide it speaks the time. The hours come in low notes. Each quarter is a doubled note. The minutes past the quarter come in high notes. He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century. He used to say that a watch which cannot tell the truth about the time has no business on anyone's wrist.

MATTHEY: Where did you go when you left the atelier?

MLLE RUEDI: Straight down to the kitchen. I stayed there with Rosa from the time I came down until after the temple struck eleven. In the kitchen I compared my watch with Rosa's clock. Her clock was exactly fifteen minutes fast. She keeps it that way on purpose, so that nothing in her kitchen is ever late.

MATTHEY: Did you hear anything from the rest of the house?

MLLE RUEDI: From the kitchen we heard Madame's piano begin at twelve minutes to eleven by the kitchen clock. It stopped at one minute past eleven by the kitchen clock. Madame plays well. I have heard her many times, and I know the sound of her hands on the keys.

MATTHEY: Is there anything you have not told me that you think I should know?

MLLE RUEDI: Only what I have told you, Monsieur. He was exact in everything he did, and he was exact about his watches, and I would like that remembered.

MATTHEY: Thank you, Mademoiselle. That will be all for now. Please ask Rosa to come in.
